the development of methods for the description of polymer structure and for the analysis of structure/property relationships.
the description of molecular structure and complexity in terms of topology.
the development of methods to describe polymer structure in a manner that is both quantitative and intuitive.

the topological indices are a powerful and useful method for the description of polymer structure.
the complexity indices are sensitive to the branching architecture, but are not necessarily sensitive to the degree of branching.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the topological indices are useful for describing the complexity of polyolefin branching patterns.
the complexity of a polyolefin is determined by a combination of the number of branches, the molecular weight of the branches, and the degree of clustering of branches.
the complexity of a polymer molecule is a function of the number and length of branches, and the position and clustering of the branches on the backbone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complexity of a polymer structure is not simply a function of molecular weight.
topology can be used as a quantitative measure of molecular complexity.
the topology of a polymer molecule is a key factor in determining its physical properties.
